In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no best optical flow technique, and that the choice of technique depends on the application at hand.
there are no good optical flow techniques.
the performance of existing optical flow methods is highly dependent on the application and the type of image sequence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the accuracy and reliability of optical flow techniques are still far from perfect, even for relatively simple sequences.
differential methods can produce good results, but only when the image is well lit and the scene has little texture.
the differential techniques perform well on synthetic images and on images that contain large, smooth regions of motion, whereas the matching techniques work better on images with fine structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for more objective evaluation of optical flow methods, including a more careful consideration of the assumptions that underly each technique.
there is no single optical flow technique that outperforms all others.
there is no one best technique.
